attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to serve DHCP on lan-a (eth2, 10.50.10.0/24) and node2 (OPNsense) to serve DHCP on lan-b (opt1/vtnet2, 10.50.20.0/24), each handing its own host a lease with itself as default gateway. node3 now obtains 10.50.10.100/24 via DHCP from node1 with default route 10.50.10.254; node4 obtains 10.50.20.100/24 via DHCP from node2 with default route 10.50.20.254. Removed prior static/manual IP assignments (NetworkManager-managed "Wired connection 2" on node3/node4 does the DHCP negotiation automatically). Resolved an OPNsense port-67 conflict where a pre-existing, non-functional Dnsmasq DHCP scope on the lan/vtnet0 interface was holding the wildcard DHCP socket and blocking Kea from binding on opt1; removed that unused Dnsmasq DHCP scope (kept DNS forwarding) so Kea DHCPv4 could bind to 10.50.20.254:67. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS via `reboot`, OPNsense via `/sbin/reboot`, both CentOS via `reboot`), each showing a changed boot identity (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime) after recovery, with lan-a/lan-b interfaces, DHCP services, and client leases/default routes all verified healthy post-restart.
